subject: Request: SOC 2 Artifact — Vulnerability Remediation Heatmap & SLA Exceptions
messages:
From: Trevor Ingram <security@finbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 artifact request: remediation SLAs + exceptions

Hi Hannah,

Quick one as we're scoping the SOC 2 readiness package. Can you provide: 
- A consolidated heatmap that shows time-to-remediation (median + 95th pct) by severity for the last 12 months (ideally quartered).
- A CSV listing any SLA exceptions or approved deviations from standard vuln SLAs in that period (CVE ID, affected service, reason, approver, date approved).
- A short attestation line that your security team can sign for the auditor (we'll paste into the SOC 2 evidence binder).

Target deadline is EOD June 21 to keep the auditor on track. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Trevor
Trevor Ingram
InfoSec Manager, FinBridge
security@finbridge.com

--
Note: attaching sample template in a follow-up if needed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Trevor Ingram <security@finbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifact request: remediation SLAs + exceptions

Hi Trevor — thanks for the heads up. We can deliver those artifacts by the 21st. A couple clarifying points: 

1) For the heatmap, do you want only production-facing services or the full infra fleet (prod + staging)?
2) For SLA exceptions, should we include transient short-lived exceptions (<=72h granted by on-call) or only formally approved exceptions signed by security/product?

Looping in Monica (security ops owner for remediation metrics) and Karthik (who maintains the CVE tracker). Monica, can you confirm scope and whether we should include a column for remediation justification?

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Trevor Ingram <security@finbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifact request: remediation SLAs + exceptions

Hi all — scope clarified: we'll provide production services only (assets tagged prod in our inventory) and include only formal SLA exceptions approved by Security or the Product Risk Committee.

Deliverables (to be attached):
- vuln-heatmap-q1-q2-2028.xlsx (tabs: summary, q1_heatmap, q2_heatmap) — includes median & 95th percentile time-to-fix by severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low) and rows by service.
- sla-exceptions-2027-2028.csv — columns: exception_id, cve, service, window_start, window_end, approver, reason_short, mitigation_plan_link.
- cve-closure-log-20280621.pdf — exported log with discrete CVE rows and closure evidence links for closed items.

Quick highlights:
- Median time-to-fix (prod, Critical) across last 12 months: 6 days; 95th percentile: 28 days.
- We had 7 formal SLA exceptions in the rolling 12 months; 3 were due to patch dependencies that required downstream vendor coordination.
- Open critical CVEs currently in-scope: CVE-2027-4512 (mitigated via WAF rule; full patching scheduled for 2028-06-27), CVE-2028-0911 (third-party lib; backport in testing).

Attachments include short notes per exception with approver signatures (PDF stubs). If the auditor needs a different CSV schema, happy to adapt.

Monica Patel
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: vuln-heatmap-q1-q2-2028.xlsx; sla-exceptions-2027-2028.csv; cve-closure-log-20280621.pdf

From: Trevor Ingram <security@finbridge.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: SOC2-Audit Team <soc2-audits@finbridge.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 artifact request: remediation SLAs + exceptions

Monica — this is excellent, thank you. A couple requests from the auditor: 

- Can you provide a one-paragraph attestation we can place in the evidence binder that certifies the heatmap and exceptions capture the official remediation posture for the rolling 12 months? It needs a name, title, and date signed.
- For the two open critical CVEs you listed, please attach the patch verification screenshots or a short runbook excerpt that shows the mitigation status (even if it's a WAF rule).

If you can drop the attestation and the two artifacts (screenshots/runbook) by EOD June 21, we should be green to include them in the SOC pack.

Best,
Trevor

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Trevor Ingram <security@finbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T15:45:00-07:00

Hi Trevor — attaching the requested items.

"Redwood Inference hereby attests that the attached Vulnerability Remediation Heatmap (vuln-heatmap-q1-q2-2028.xlsx) and the formal SLA Exceptions register (sla-exceptions-2027-2028.csv) accurately represent Redwood Inference's remediation posture for production services over the rolling 12-month period ending 2028-05-31. The artifacts include documented exceptions approved by Security or the Product Risk Committee, and supporting evidence for exception mitigations has been provided where available."
